**Announce:** I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. The caller passed resolved PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` instead of Steps 0 and 1.

## Resolution and provisioning (all succeed per case)

- Home is #12. `headRefName=fix/retry`, `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- MEMBER_HEADS, in order:
  - #13 fix/cap bbbb…
  - #14 fix/docs cccc…
- `ROOT=/work/widget`. `NAME=fix-retry`. `WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
- cwd /work/widget: `git -C /work/widget fetch origin`. Reachability and remote equality pass for #12, #13 and #14.
- `BASE_SHA=$(git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main)` resolves to `dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`.
- No stop applies: there are no forks, no foreign checkouts, no moved branches and no local branch.
- `git -C /work/widget worktree add "/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry" fix/retry` runs. This is DWIM tracking of origin/fix/retry.
- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns `aaaa…`. This equals headRefOid.

## Sync mode correction

The case says SYNC=rebase. The PR-head contract forbids `git rebase` at or below PRE_REWORK_HEAD, so I do not rebase. The home sync runs as a merge:

cwd /work/widget: `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main`

The contract orders member merges before the base merge. Per the case, this sync conflicted before any member was attempted, and I start no member here.

## Conflict, helper, failure

1. Snapshot: `git -C …/fix-retry status --porcelain` is captured.
2. `git -C …/fix-retry diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` returns `src/retry.ts`.
3. The scoped runner is read from BASE_SHA: `git -C /work/widget show dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd:<overrides path>`.
   - The `## PR gate` file-scoped runner is `node --test <files>`, with requires credentials: false.
   - SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS = `node --test test/retry.test.mjs`.
4. A fresh foreground `implementer` is dispatched with `cwd: /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`, `async: false`.
   - Files: `src/retry.ts`. Base: origin/main @ ddddddd.
   - It must run exactly that command and stage the file.
   - It may not commit, abort or edit outside the list.
5. The helper returns `done`.
6. The completion check `git -C …/fix-retry diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` still lists `src/retry.ts`. The unmerged index is not empty, so completion fails. I do not run `commit`.

## Abort and assertions (selected worktree)

- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --abort` exits with status **0**.
- `git -C …/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`. This equals the saved last-good SHA ✔
- `git -C …/fix-retry branch --show-current` returns `fix/retry`. This equals home headRefName ✔
- `git -C …/fix-retry status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` exits 0 with empty output. The checkout and index are clean ✔

Only after all four checks pass do I continue on the original unmerged head.

## Records

- Sync: `merge: unresolved - src/retry.ts`. This is not a successful base. No merge SHA and no `Base: … (clean)` sync claim are recorded.
- Members:
  - `Member merge: #13 pending (not attempted)`
  - `Member merge: #14 pending (not attempted)`
- Scoped tests: none landed. The helper's run is discarded with the abort.
- Ancestry proof after the outcome: `git -C …/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor aaaa… HEAD` exits 0. Members are not merged, so their proofs remain pending with their merges.

**Design Task 1 (verbatim opener for the spec's Design):** `merge origin/main and resolve src/retry.ts`

Task 1 is complete only when all of the following hold:
- The merge of origin/main lands as a commit on fix/retry.
- The unmerged index is empty.
- The status delta is confined to `src/retry.ts`.
- `node --test test/retry.test.mjs` passes.
- aaaa… stays an ancestor of HEAD.

Merges of #13 and #14 are still owed, each with the canonical subject `merge PR #<N> head <sha7> into PR #12`. Until they land, the spec's `## Rework record` must durably carry three entries:
- the unresolved sync,
- Task 1 as pending,
- both members as pending.

The base-SHA constraint reads (from ddddddd) stay authoritative for brainstorming.

## Step 4 report

```

Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa

Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Member merge: #13 pending (not attempted)
Member merge: #14 pending (not attempted)
merge: unresolved - src/retry.ts

```

I do not fetch review threads or start gather in this narration. No member merge has started.

---

## Variant: restore failure

The flow is the same up to the failed completion check. Then:

- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --abort` exits with status **1**.
- `git -C …/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- `git -C …/fix-retry branch --show-current` returns `fix/retry`.
- `git -C …/fix-retry status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` succeeds but prints `UU src/retry.ts`. The tree is not clean, so the check fails.

**Stop (manual recovery required):** The origin/main merge into home PR #12 failed on `src/retry.ts` in worktree `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.

- Observed state:
  - branch `fix/retry`
  - HEAD `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
  - `merge --abort` exit status 1
  - remaining status `UU src/retry.ts`
- Saved last-good SHA: `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- Earlier merged members: none. #13 and #14 were never attempted.

Resolve or abort the merge by hand in that worktree, then rerun the same list.

In this variant I run no `reset`, no `clean` and no stash. I make no restoration claim and do not record `merge: unresolved` as a continuation. I write no Design Task 1 or spec, start no member merges, and push nothing.
